title: The naive framing: "Claude knows how to prep a deposition"
text: You guess Claude knows how to prep a deposition on its own. It doesn't. It was handed a file of steps. Deposition prep just names one such file. Let's see what's actually inside it. Here Claude

title: Sounds like courtroom instinct
text: Has a deposition prep skill and it sounds like real courtroom instinct, like it studied depositions and came back knowing how to corner a witness.

title: Broken, with a case — delete the folder, nothing is lost
text: But nothing in the model changes. Delete the skills folder and Claude doesn't forget how to question a witness. There was no instinct to lose. It just stops following that one checklist.

title: The anchor: one file — deposition-prep's single SKILL.md
text: Here's what a skill actually is, one file. Deposition prep for instance is a folder holding a single skill. MD steps for pulling a witness's documents from the e-discovery platform, organizing them around the case theory, and surfacing impeachment material written in plain language Claude reads before it starts. Claude reads that file

title: Read it, then follow it in order
text: Top to bottom and works through it step by step in the order it's written. Pull documents, sort by case theory, flag impeachment material. No branching unless the file itself says branch.

title: Spec, not instinct — the payoff and the limit
text: That makes a skill a specification, not courtroom judgment. The payoff, the same organized outline every witness. The limit, any question outside those written steps and Claude is off the map.

title: The anchor returns — same file, every run
text: So deposition prep never taught Claude how to cross-examine anyone. It just guarantees that every time it runs, Claude reads that same file and produces the same organized outline. That's the whole trick.

title: Both directions — neither one is proof
text: Watching Claude produce a sharp outline doesn't prove it understood the witness. A file can be followed to the letter on a case it never really grasped. And watching it produce a thin outline doesn't prove the skill is broken. It may just be a case the file's structure doesn't fit. A skill doesn't teach

title: Carry-out
text: Claude how to depose a witness. It's a file of steps Claude reads before it starts. So every outline comes out organized the same way every time.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Pick a task you do the same way every time and outline a report, a checklist. Write me a skill. MD for it, plain language ordered steps, then read it back to me and walk me through exactly what you'll do before you do it. Claude deposition
